original_finding.provenance: Original same-author source-preparation concern transcribed from collaboration message; no capability probe or execution occurred. Native visibility assertion is for actual Astra to verify/resolve, not assumed acceptance.
original_finding.original_author_message: 一个 source-only 能力边界先说明：stdlib signal.getsignal(SIGUSR2) 可拒绝已登记的 Python custom handler，但 faulthandler.register 的既有 native 注册没有公开查询 API。计划要 native SIGUSR2 原 ownership 检查/restore；若要求证明不存在任意先存 native sigaction，这不能由纯 stdlib public API 单独证明。拟记录 getSignal 可见原 handler、当前 hook 冲突、native-preexisting-registration 未可观察，并只 unregister 本插件成功注册；请确认这属于本合同的 visibility limit，还是需要实际 Astra 澄清。尚未安装/执行 observer。

affected_contract.lifecycle: Require exact command/node/output gate. At collection completion require exactly the literal one UTC-memory item. Never invoke --collect-only separately. Before behavior, reject existing non-null sys/threading profile hooks or existing SIGUSR2 custom owner instead of overriding unrelated observers. Record observed coverage, including existing threads not covered by threading.setprofile.
affected_contract.stack_method: At pytest session start register stdlib faulthandler SIGUSR2, all_threads=True, chain=False, writing to exclusive stacks.raw; record native ready receipt <=4KiB with PID, command and plugin pin. No SIGALRM use and no new Python sampler thread. Parent only signals its verified child PID after readiness. Do not use ptrace, gdb, native instrumentation, /proc/mem or external commands.
affected_contract.stack_schedule: 19 fixed request opportunities at child-start +30,60,...,570s; each only once, no catch-up burst/retry. Parent append request sequence, requested/actual monotonic_ns, PID, expected source and pre-signal stack-file size before os.kill(SIGUSR2). Read only this explicit ready JSON <=4KiB (nofollow stable path) while child lives; otherwise metadata-only live artifact walks. No ready receipt by a sample -> record missing, no signal. Subsequent sampled file sizes define raw offset bounds only; request != completed stack sample. Parser reports raw partials and uncertain grouping, never manufactures ack/timestamp.

original_finding.ROOT_disposition: Do not silently downgrade ownership requirement or add ctypes/sigaction. Pause affected native signal ownership/registration lifecycle source until actual Astra decision; unaffected profiling and parent capture preparation may continue.

verified_cause: The R354 native signal ownership wording was stronger than getsignal/public faulthandler query visibility. Blind register/unregister could overwrite native owners. No product or runtime failure occurred.

authority_sources.readout: getsignal returns Python-visible handler values including None for handlers not installed from Python; it is not an API to return arbitrary current native sigaction structures or handler identity.

register installs a user-signal traceback handler; chain controls calling the previous handler. unregister reports whether faulthandler registered that signal. The output descriptor must remain valid for registration lifetime. No documented public registered-user-signal query is provided.

authority_sources.source_reference: faulthandler_register lines698-727; register_py lines785-844; unregister lines846-879; finalization lines1253-1274
authority_sources.readout: Reference CPython implementation saves previous native action on first registration, can reuse an enabled entry without another sigaction call, and unregister restores its saved previous action without comparing the current action pointer. This source reference is not claimed as a verified build-source mapping for the installed binary.
SigCgt/SigIgn/SigBlk expose caught/ignored/blocked bitmasks; SigPnd and ShdPnd expose pending masks. These snapshots do not identify handler addresses or provide atomic compare-and-install.

decision: Retain native SIGUSR2 stack requests only for this fresh controlled single-command child, with main-only registration epoch, kernel disposition snapshots, explicit exclusive-use assumption and coordinated retirement. Do not claim arbitrary native sigaction ownership proof. Reject unknown/conflicting startup state before behavior; do not silently proceed with registration when checks are unavailable.

control_contract.lock: Use one exclusively created regular nofollow signal-control.lock, stable inode, fcntl.flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB around all signal-state transitions and parent eligibility-check+os.kill. No polling lock acquisition loop: contention skips that request; teardown contention records deferred cleanup. Do not replace lock inode. State JSON <=4096 bytes, exact command/PID/start identity/plugin pin/epoch/state and last observed masks. Atomic replacement of only the state JSON is permitted under the lock; immutable ready receipt remains evidence, never a permanent send authorization.
control_contract.exclusive_use: After eligibility, only this plugin may register/unregister SIGUSR2 and only this parent may send the19 planned SIGUSR2 requests. Same controlled command imports only frozen allowed plugins/test dependencies; no external owner or asynchronous mutation is presumed supported. Finite source review found no explicit SIGUSR2/register/unregister in18 directly pinned Python sources; it does not prove all transitive native code. New known native signal writer or evidence of concurrent mutation rejects applicability.
control_contract.race_limit: /proc status reads and registration are not atomic. A single native thread and no application/callback between final precheck and registration reduce the race; they do not prove absence of arbitrary asynchronous C mutation. Observed caught/ignored bits establish a snapshot class, not a handler pointer. Report this contract/limit explicitly; never claim full native ownership restored solely from masks or getsignal.

registration: At original pytest_sessionstart before collection/test behavior, after original R235 prerequisite has completed, verify main Python thread and main native TID==PID. Native registration is only attempted once during the already reserved command.

Before installing profiles or a signal handler, acquire control lock nonblocking; take two bounded /proc/<self-pid>/status and /proc/<self-pid>/task name observations around eligibility. Require native task set exactly {main TID}, Threads==1, stable PID/start identity, TracerPid==0; do not substitute threading.enumerate for kernel threads.

For bit 1 << (int(SIGUSR2)-1), require Python getsignal is exactly SIG_DFL (not None/SIG_IGN/callable), SigCgt==0, SigIgn==0, SigBlk==0, SigPnd==0 and ShdPnd==0 for that bit. Preserve raw parsed fields and monotonic observation times. Missing field, parse error, any conflict, second thread, or changed identity rejects; never clear an existing handler or ignored disposition to make it eligible.

Still in that main-only lock interval, block only SIGUSR2 with pthread_sigmask(SIG_BLOCK,{SIGUSR2}) and retain the returned full prior mask. This is the sole permitted temporary mask change, not a product clock/authority change. Recheck no pending SIGUSR2, one native task, same Python SIG_DFL, clear caught/ignored bits before register. No product calls/imports or callbacks between final check and register.

Open exclusive stacks.raw, keep its descriptor live. Call faulthandler.register(SIGUSR2,file=fd,all_threads=True,chain=False) once. Mark own_registration_success only on successful return. Postcheck caught bit set, ignored bit clear, unchanged Python-visible SIG_DFL, one native task and no pending target signal. Restore precisely the saved thread mask; verify target unblocked. Only then publish READY and immutable ready evidence, while holding the lock.

Any eligibility/registration/postcheck failure yields REJECTED, no ready/send permission and no behavioral execution. Record actual evidence; do not call unregister as a capability probe, register twice, force SIG_DFL or alter unrelated signals. If partial installation/pending state cannot be safely unwound, keep descriptor and report unresolved state for owned-process termination rather than blind restoration.
parent_requests: Keep exactly19 original scheduled opportunities; no retries or catch-up. Each acquires control lock nonblocking within original monitor headroom and requires live child identity, matching READY epoch and immutable ready pin. Re-read exact state JSON (<=4KiB); cached READY is insufficient.

Within the same lock, read /proc/<child-pid>/status <=64KiB. Require caught target bit set, ignored/leader-blocked/pending target bits clear and stable PID/start identity. This is a send-eligibility check, not handler-pointer verification. Failure/missingness records skipped request and invalidates native sampling; do not send or repair handler.

Append original request metadata before sending; send only os.kill(verified child PID,SIGUSR2). Release lock after syscall. No broadcast/process-group SIGUSR2. No file growth or kill return is treated as completed traceback or exclusive-owner proof.

If child retires or exits, no further sends. Unexpected state conflicts reject affected diagnostic applicability, with all existing cleanup/independent capture retained. Do not allocate a replacement signal or sampler.
retirement: Sessionfinish/unconfigure share one idempotent retirement path. Acquire same lock nonblocking; mark CLOSED before any unregister so no new parent request can pass. If lock is busy, do not block teardown or unregister/close stack fd; record deferred retirement and retain fd through process lifetime. Parent must also stop sends after it observes process exit.

Only if own_registration_success, no observed ownership drift, exact same epoch/PID, current Python handler still SIG_DFL, caught bit set, ignored bit clear, and task set again exactly {main}, temporarily block SIGUSR2 and recheck both pending masks are clear under CLOSED lock. This excludes already submitted controlled-parent signals; no pending signal is drained or fabricated.

If all conditions hold, call faulthandler.unregister(SIGUSR2) once; require True. Verify kernel caught/ignored bits now clear, Python-visible SIG_DFL and unchanged one-thread identity, then restore exactly the prior thread mask. Retain raw pre/post facts and only claim observed default disposition under the controlled-use contract, not arbitrary native structure equality. Close stack fd only after successful unregister and coherent postchecks.

If task count>1, pending state, unknown native ownership, lost lock, postcheck discrepancy or any uncertainty exists, do not force signal.signal, clear another handler, re-register or drain pending signals. Record RETIRED_PROCESS_EXIT_ONLY, keep the stack descriptor valid until controlled process exit. Restore a temporary thread mask only where still safe with our handler installed; otherwise record mask restoration UNKNOWN and rely on owned termination. No handler restoration success is claimed.

If no own successful registration, never invoke unregister. After timeout/forced termination, Python teardown is not assumed to have run: ROOT accepts only actual process-group reaping and retained missingness; signal restoration remains UNOBSERVED. The disposed child is never reused. No native fd is reused while a potentially live handler references it.

bounds.guard_budget_rule: All work consumes existing child/monitor/cleanup/capture windows; never grants extra elapsed time. Child checks record elapsed and fail eligibility on overrun; parent guards shorten to remaining HEAD/child deadline. fcntl lock is nonblocking. A blocked kernel metadata read remains bounded by existing outer owned-process timeout, no new SIGALRM.
